Trends 2026-11-02

⬛ Overview · 🟪 AI Agents · 🟦 AI Models & Labs · 🟨 Data Engineering · 🟫 Trends

Sources: GitHub Trending + GitHub Search API + OpenRouter + npm + Hugging Face + arXiv + Hacker News + Lobste.rs + Dev.to | Generated: 2026-11-02 05:48 UTC

Highlights

  • OpenRouter usage on 2026-11-01: deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-20261017 is #1 with 48.08T tokens.
  • JetBrains/thinkrail gained 5,760 stars in 7 days (+454%), the largest absolute and relative gain among Coding Agents rows.
  • pbakaus/impeccable gained 12,017 stars in 7 days (+14%), the largest absolute gain across the four GitHub category tables.

Agents & coding tools

🚀 Agent & Coding Tool Radar

New tools (🆕: created or listed in the last 14 days) first, then each source's top movers; 🔥 also on last week's Trends page. OpenRouter: the app's rank this week / this month among OpenRouter apps, its tokens in the last 7 days. npm: downloads in the last 7 days. OpenRouter and npm "vs previous week": against the row's figure on last week's page, none when it was not there. GitHub: total stars (stars gained in the last 7 days, % on a week ago).

haydenschmitty/floorplan GitHub 🆕 1,890 (+1,890) floorplan generates an interactive plain-English map of a codebase, drawn by Claude or Codex.
MiniMax-AI/mcode-stack GitHub 🆕 501 (+501) mcode-stack contains the workflows and skills the MiniMax Code team uses to build MiniMax Code, open sourced for installation and use.

Skills: PRs and requests this week

Source: anthropics/skills

  • #2110 adds --non-trigger-threshold and symmetric pass logic to skill-creator eval scripts; still open.
  • #2097 makes aggregate_benchmark.py discover eval directories by contents instead of the eval-* glob; still open.
  • #2086 supports separate trigger-rate thresholds for should-trigger and should-not-trigger cases; still open.

Merged this week

  • #2087 updates mcp-builder to v2 of the MCP TypeScript SDK, pointing new servers at v2 packages while retaining the v1 guide.

Requests

  • #518 reports eval-loop rough edges in skill-creator, including grading paths, Bash blocking, and aggregate_benchmark.py bugs.
  • #2051 asks how the model chooses among multiple skills with overlapping trigger conditions.
  • #2054 requests a way to audit which installed skills actually triggered in past sessions.

Takeaway

The open PRs and issues all target more reliable, observable, and configurable skill triggering and evaluation in Claude Code.

Research

Paper Summary
ShutdownMod: Turning Any Trajectory into a Shutdown Evaluation ShutdownMod turns any agent trajectory into a shutdown evaluation by injecting a shutdown request into the agent's context and recording the response, using a signature-verification tool to distinguish trusted interventions from unauthorized injections, and evaluates seven models on 50 tasks or recorded sessions.
A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator presents an LLM agent loop built for accelerators rarely seen by frontier LLMs, demonstrated by optimizing three Gemma-4-12B decode kernels on the FuriosaAI RNGD NPU over 12 days on a shared, scarce device.
FlexA-Mem: Budget-Adaptive Agentic Memory for LLM Agents FlexA-Mem proposes a general budget-adaptive agentic memory that writes each unit of history once.
Task Success Is Not Enough: Side-effect-Aware Evaluation of Tool-Using Language Model Agents Task Success Is Not Enough introduces SABench, a side-effect-aware benchmark of 201 email, calendar, and ticket tasks crossing four state structures, to evaluate collateral damage beyond task success.
Does Your Generalist Skill Optimizer Really Incentivize Agentic Tasks? Rethinking Skill Optimization via Bipartite Attribution Does Your Generalist Skill Optimizer Really Incentivize Agentic Tasks? Rethinking Skill Optimization via Bipartite Attribution introduces BiPA, which replays an optimizer's acceptance rule on candidates identical to its seed and records each episode as a bipartite graph of turns and the text they read.
Spine: Compiling Subtask Trees into Structured Context for Long-Horizon Coding Agents Spine introduces an interface and runtime for compiling subtask trees into structured context for long-horizon coding agents.
SWE-Clar: Can Coding Agents Clarify Incomplete Client Requirements and Deliver Greenfield Software? SWE-Clar introduces a benchmark for greenfield software development in which clarification precedes code implementation and effectiveness is assessed through explicit tests of requirement understanding.
WebViSE: Scaling Visual Design Intelligence from the Open Web for LLM Website Generation WebViSE introduces Website-derived Visual Skill Extraction, a framework that automatically abstracts open-web website implementations into reusable visual skills for LLM website generation.
HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency HarnessMM introduces a method for improving harness token efficiency through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement, using a controller that reuses resolved decisions to replace later reasoning callbacks while actor weights remain fixed.
RepoTrace: Improving Requirement Tracing in Multi-Round Agent Interactions RepoTrace analyzes 2,656 agent trajectories in EvoCode-Bench, identifies requirement focus misalignment as a recurring failure pattern, and proposes a requirement-driven repository understanding approach.

Research

Paper Summary
nnInteractive Agent: General-Purpose AI Agents as 3D Image Annotators The paper shows that general-purpose AI agents can take over 3D annotation work without additional training by interpreting plain-language requests, locating targets, prompting nnInteractive, and inspecting and correcting 3D results.
SWE-VERIFIER: Selective Verification for Cost-Efficient Coding Agents SWE-Verifier introduces a lightweight generative model that selectively triggers candidate sampling and verification by scoring a coding agent's proposed action to determine when additional sampling is needed.
Governed Self-Evolution for Autonomous Investing: A Multi-Agent LLM System with an Invariant Core Steward is a multi-agent LLM system for autonomous investing with an invariant core where nine role-specialised agents jointly decide, with four analysts emitting typed reports from diverse data sources for a Portfolio Manager to set target positions.
Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution Environment Duels presents a dynamic agentic benchmark where models author interactive environments with privileged hints and solve them, revealing that solving and authoring capabilities are distinct across nine frontier LLMs.
MAPS: Macro-Adaptive Parallel Reasoning for Regulating Search Momentum in Retrieval-Augmented Generation MAPS characterizes the evolution of query intent in retrieval-augmented generation by introducing macro-adaptive parallel reasoning to regulate search momentum and address redundant sub-queries and insufficiently diverse exploration.
PAUSE: Search-Free Steering of Coding Agents Before Their First Source-Code Edit PAUSE proposes a single planning intervention to steer coding agents before their first source-code edit, which occurs at a median of 60% trajectory progress after exploration, bug reproduction, and testing.
Harnessing Language Models as Optimization Modeling Agents OPTICYCLE and OPTISTATE are two lightweight inference harnesses for optimization modeling that achieve competitive performance on nine benchmarks comprising 2,634 problems without additional training.
SWE-DIVE: Multi-Turn Coding Agent Evaluation with Dynamic User Simulation SWE-DIVE introduces a multi-turn coding agent evaluation framework with dynamic user simulation to benchmark agents on iterative, less-structured interactions beyond one-shot GitHub issues.
Beyond Watching and Searching: Benchmarking Agents for Video-centered Deep Research Reports The paper introduces Video-Centered Deep Research Report Generation where agents identify research questions, retrieve multimodal evidence, and produce interactive reports linked to video moments, presenting a skill-based workflow for this task.
LLM2Cert: LLM Synthesis of Certificates with SMT/Lean Verification LLM2Cert synthesizes Lyapunov functions and barrier certificates using LLMs and verifies them with SMT/Lean solvers, addressing limitations of numerical solvers that require relaxations, are conservative, or scale poorly.
